panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real clinical photograph of severe LAD I showing skin lesions without pus, consistent with captioned disease manifestation. [raw subtype: LAD I] B: Real clinical photograph of severe LAD I showing non-purulent necrotic skin lesions, matching the caption. [raw subtype: LAD I]

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Frontal facial clinical photo of LAD II patient described in caption as showing long eyelashes and broad depressed nasal bridge; no vocabulary finding matches so captured as proposed_findings. [raw subtype: II] B: Palmar clinical photo described in caption as showing simian crease as clinical stigmata of LAD II patient. [raw subtype: II] C: Dorsal feet photo described as dorsally positioned second toes, listed as LAD II stigmata. [raw subtype: II] D: Profile facial view showing depressed nasal bridge profile in LAD II patient. [raw subtype: II] E: Intrauterine ultrasound at 28th week gestation stated to show depressed nasal bridge in same LAD II patient. [raw subtype: II]
panels.attribution_text: Marquardt et al. Leukocyte adhesion deficiency II syndrome, a generalized defect in fucose metabolism.. The Journal of pediatrics 1999. doi:10.1016/s0022-3476(99)70281-7. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical stigmata. Long eyelashes, a broad and depressed nasal bridge, a simian crease, and dorsally positioned second toes are the clinical stigmata of the patient with LAD II. The depressed nasal bridge was already seen on intrauterine ultrasonographic investigation in the 28th week of gestation (lower right panel) .
